# How This Book Is Written {.unnumbered}

A book about AI-assisted engineering should be candid about how it was made.
I am developing this manuscript in public while both the subject and the
argument are still changing. Thinking in the open lets me test the synthesis
against current research and reader feedback rather than wait for the field to
settle. It also keeps me returning to the evidence, examples, and claims as new
work appears. A public draft gives me a way to find and correct weak claims
sooner.

I use generative systems throughout this work. They assist with searching for
and organizing candidate material, proposing outlines, offering alternative
formulations when an explanation is unclear, and checking whether connections
across the manuscript remain consistent. I also use them to challenge an
assumption or identify a passage that needs closer review. These outputs are
leads and drafts, not evidence.

The final choices are mine. I select the sources, read and interpret the
evidence, verify the claims, decide which connections hold, revise the prose,
and determine the argument. I discard fluent material when a source does not
support it or a connection fails under closer inspection. The tools widen the
possibilities I consider. This experience has reinforced the book's argument
that generative systems may extend engineering work while human judgment
remains central to deciding what a result supports.

This remains a working manuscript, and I expect it to change as the argument
and evidence improve. Publishing the draft openly gives readers context for
judging its present state. Responsibility for it remains mine.

Vijay Janapa Reddi
